clue.text: Concerning the study of good food (no topping) - it's great!

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so having no topping means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: Concerning the study of good food
blocks.note: gastronomy is the study of good eating, and this is its adjective

explanation.surface: A food critic exclaims that a book about fine dining, sadly missing its garnish, is still wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the G from GASTRONOMIC to leave ASTRONOMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic, like astronomical, describes something enormous, as vast as the distances between stars.

clue.text: Doubter acting so odd

indicators.note: something odd is irregular and out of its usual shape, so these letters are put into a strange new order

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sceptic is behaving strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that the existence of God can be known, so is a doubter in religious matters.

clue.text: Conceit at the book fair?

blocks.note: surface reading: an author showing off at a publishing trade fair
setter's reading: the fair named in a book, the one in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress that gave Thackeray his novel title

explanation.surface: Authors preening themselves at a literary trade fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The fair in the book is Vanity Fair, from Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress and Thackeray's novel; its first word means conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity is excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements, which is exactly what conceit means.

clue.text: Trophy for working horse, worn out

indicators.note: something worn on the outside covers what is beneath, so the horse word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: gee-gee, a childish word for a horse, abbreviated
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A prize awarded to a tired old workhorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' looks like it means exhausted, but it says GG is worn on the outside of ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or award, so it serves as an informal word for a trophy.

clue.text: Many by Spey caber-tossing - in virtual reality

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so these letters land in a different order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Crowds watch caber-tossing by the River Spey at a Highland games, but it is all a computer simulation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a Scottish river, and tossing the caber (a long tree trunk) is a Highland games event; 'caber-tossing' splits so that 'tossing' works on SPEY CABER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional world of computer networks, a virtual realm rather than physical reality.

clue.text: Made much of the upside-down puddings

indicators.note: in a down entry turning a word upside-down means reading it from the bottom up

blocks.note: puddings is the British word for desserts

explanation.surface: Someone fussed over upside-down cakes, like a pineapple upside-down pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: STRESSED read backwards is DESSERTS, a well-known reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, so stressed means emphasised or made much of.

clue.text: Lhasa mosaic hiding Asian titbit

indicators.note: the words keep something concealed inside them, so look within the run of letters

blocks.note: spanning the end of the city name and the start of the tiling word

explanation.surface: A tiled mosaic in Lhasa, Tibet's capital, conceals a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a small fried pastry from South Asia, a savoury snack or titbit.

clue.text: Ditch large corporation boss

blocks.note: first meaning: a channel or embankment for water
second meaning: Greg ..., once Director-General of the BBC, known in Britain as the Corporation

explanation.surface: A demand to sack the chief executive of a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' reads as a verb meaning get rid of, but it is a noun. The BBC is often called 'the Corporation', and Greg Dyke ran it from 2000 to 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is a drainage ditch or bank, and Greg Dyke was head of the British Broadcasting Corporation.

clue.text: Underwriter's gesture to a Conservative

blocks.note: a sign is a gesture
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An insurance underwriter waves to a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To underwrite originally meant to sign underneath, so one who signs a document, a signatory, is literally an underwriter.

clue.text: Waterworks close due to rent anomaly, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word just before it, so take its final letter

blocks.note: a rent is a tear or rip
the final letter of anomaly

explanation.surface: A water company's plant is shut down because of an irregularity in its rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterworks' is slang for tears, so 'waterworks close' means about to cry. 'Rent' is a rip, read as TEAR, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teary is on the verge of crying, so the waterworks, meaning tears, are near at hand.

clue.text: Carnival city can get German revelling

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, famous for its carnival
a tin is a can
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: The carnival in Rio lets a German visitor party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb 'is able to' but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioting can mean unrestrained merrymaking, as in a riot of fun, so it matches noisy revelling.

clue.text: Look at Archer's comeback - not a pretty sight

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the Archer's name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
Eros, the Greek god of love, is armed with bow and arrows

explanation.surface: Seeing Jeffrey Archer return to public life is an unwelcome view.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer looks like the politician-novelist Jeffrey Archer, but it is Eros, the winged archer of love.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, so it is literally not a pretty sight.

clue.text: Daft teachers go to the limits of technology

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters of the next word

blocks.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
the first and last letters of technology

explanation.surface: Foolish teachers push technology as far as it can go.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is informal for crazy or foolish, a close synonym of daft.

clue.text: It's designed for ablutions by western tree bear

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
the ash is a tree
to bear something is to stand it, tolerate it

explanation.surface: A western tree is planned to be a bear's bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb, to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A washstand is a piece of furniture holding a basin and jug for washing yourself, the ablutions of the clue.

clue.text: Sussex town made famous by Longfellow?

blocks.note: surface reading: a place celebrated by the American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
setter's reading: a long fellow, the tall chalk hill figure called the Long Man, cut into the downs by this village

explanation.surface: A town in Sussex owes its fame to a poem by Longfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in southern England; the Long Man of Wilmington is a huge chalk figure of a man on the hillside there.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilmington is a village in East Sussex, best known for the Long Man figure on the neighbouring hill.

clue.text: Power pack for empty guns

blocks.note: a dry well or bottle is empty
a battery is a group of artillery guns

explanation.surface: Someone wants a power supply for guns that have run out of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry battery is a cell with paste rather than liquid electrolyte, a portable source of electrical power.

clue.text: Portillo, perhaps, shows uncontrolled dismay as bloomer's revealed

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild and fall into a new order

blocks.note: Michael Portillo is a British former Conservative minister and TV presenter; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of the name
the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician cannot hide his alarm when his embarrassing gaffe comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, which suits the politician, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, and anything that flowers can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Weapon of mass destruction found in a grave by angry mob

indicators.note: an angry crowd is unruly and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a tomb is a grave
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deadly weapon is discovered buried in a grave beside a furious crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom bomb is a nuclear weapon, the textbook example of a weapon able to destroy on a mass scale.

clue.text: Terrorists and North way in to to arms scandal

blocks.note: the Irish Republican Army
N is the abbreviation for North
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Terrorists from the north find an entrance into an arms deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published repeats 'to'. Irangate, or Iran-Contra, was the 1980s US scandal over secret arms sales to Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Irangate was the Reagan-era affair in which weapons were sold covertly to Iran, a political scandal about arms.

clue.text: Acid-like shower covers Rio

indicators.note: a shower scatters things about as they fall, so these letters come down in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Acid rain falls over Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' reads as rain, the subject of the sentence, but it tells you to scatter the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acids eat away at metal and stone, and corrosive describes any substance with that destructive, eating action.

clue.text: Curtis Strange's sort of course, they say

definitions.note: 'course, they say' sounds like coarse, so this means rough or unrefined

indicators.note: a strange arrangement is an unfamiliar one, so the name before it is rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The kind of golf course the American champion Curtis Strange prefers.
explanation.walkthrough: Curtis Strange is a golfer, so 'course' suggests a golf course; 'they say' turns it into its sound-alike coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means simple and unrefined, as country things are thought to be, which is a sort of coarse.

clue.text: Climber needs a fix to make the return

indicators.note: making a return means going back the way you came, so the pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to nail something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs a fixed rope or peg to get back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a long woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees toward the light.

clue.text: General method is slack

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: The general's approach is lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room for manoeuvre or allowance, the same as slack given in a rope or schedule.

clue.text: Mixed beans go into food container

indicators.note: mixing stirs the contents together, so these letters lose their original order

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A mixture of beans is tipped into a lunchbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a bag of feed hung over a horse's head, so it holds the animal's food.

clue.text: Refusal to sanction a recess

blocks.note: no is a refusal
to OK something is to approve or sanction it

explanation.surface: Parliament declines to approve a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' suggests a parliamentary holiday, but it is an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner or alcove in a room, which is what a recess in a wall is.

clue.text: Father figure has a load to carry

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
eight is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A dad has a heavy burden to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father figure' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods transported by lorry, ship or train, a cargo load to be carried.

clue.text: Initially foreign editors expose government people

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of foreign
ed is short for editor, so eds are editors

explanation.surface: Overseas newspaper editors uncover state officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Feds is US slang for federal agents, such as the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Feds are officers of the US federal government, especially federal law-enforcement agents.

clue.text: Investigator's uncertainty after taking love drug

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a private investigator
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A detective is unsure after taking a love potion.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic made from poppy sap, an addictive drug.

clue.text: Ex-graduate painter

blocks.note: ex means former, old
a master is a holder of a master's degree, a graduate

explanation.surface: A former university student who now paints.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Master is a great European artist from before about 1800, or one of their paintings.
